body: This also results in `NgControl.statusChanges` etc being null. This is a major blocker for us updating to Ivy.

I was able to repro this with rc.1

The odd thing is that the `NgControl` has a different shape with Ivy than without:

`enableIvy: false`:
![Screen Shot 2019-11-08 at 5 56 02 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/216296/68521002-75316780-0251-11ea-86dd-0355977cc897.png)

`enableIvy: true`:
![Screen Shot 2019-11-08 at 5 55 48 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/216296/68521005-79f61b80-0251-11ea-8ad3-e53315a1f47f.png)


Notice that the `control` prop is missing with Ivy and that the object has `__ngContext__` and `__ngSimpleChanges__` props. Is this expected?

issue.title: Custom directive - @Self() has null valueChanged observable property during ngOnInit

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Indicates than the issue relates to something that worked in a previous version

issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package _Angular 9 RC2_ The issue is caused by package @angular/core@next ### Is this a regression? Yes, the previous version in which this bug was not present was: v8.2.14 ### Description I have upgraded a project from `v8.2.14` to `v9.0.0-rc.2` . After the upgrade, a custom directive throws an error trying to access a null property on the control. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction https://github.com/JamesHough/angular9-directive-error.git The repo attached has a single custom directive `CleanUnusualCharactersDirective` which has a reference to the control in the constructor: `@Self() private control: NgControl` When this directive executes `ngOnInit()` then the property "valueChanges" is null ``` ngOnInit(): void { this.subscriptions = this.control.valueChanges .pipe(distinctUntilChanged()) .subscribe((v: string) => this.cleanInput(v)); } ``` This repo has the previous working version on Angular 8.2.14 in the commit history. ## 🔥 Exception or Error Error in the JavaScript console: 

core.js:6161 ERROR TypeError: Cannot read property 'pipe' of null
    at CleanUnusualCharactersDirective.ngOnInit (clean-unusual-characters.directive.ts:34)
